claim: Let \(s(m)=m\) when \(m\) is prime, and let \(s(m)=m/\operatorname{lpf}(m)\) otherwise, where \(\operatorname{lpf}(m)\) is the least prime factor of \(m\). Define \(C_0=\{1\}\) and \(C_{n+1}=C_n\cup\{s(a+b):a,b\in C_n\}\). Let \(M_n=\max C_n\), let \(R_n\) be the least prime absent from \(C_n\), and let \(Q_n\) be the prime immediately preceding \(R_n\). Then \(Q_n=M_n\) for every \(1\le n\le 26\), while at generation \(27\) one has \(|C_{27}|=170224\), \(M_{27}=262331\), \(R_{27}=262321\), and \(Q_{27}=262313\). Hence generation \(27\) is the first stage at which \(C_n\) fails to contain every prime up to its maximum. In particular, \(262321\notin C_{27}\) but \(262331\in C_{27}\); the latter is generated by \(100188+162143=262331\) with both summands in \(C_{26}\).

correctness.rationale: Exact reconstruction from the recurrence proves the finite statement. The bitset union of shifts is exactly the sumset \(C_n+C_n\); an integer least-prime-factor sieve evaluates the subprime map on every attainable sum. Published cardinalities through generation \(27\) match as an external cross-check. The positive witness for \(262331\) and the exhaustive pair-sum exclusion for \(262321\), together with \(2M_{26}<2R_{27}\), separately certify the decisive boundary. No infinite claim is inferred from finite computation.

value.rationale: The first separation of \(Q_n\) and \(M_n\) is a natural exact invariant singled out by the notation and asymptotic theorem of the 2026 source. It gives the earliest boundary where the tempting stronger property 'every prime up to the maximum is present' fails, and explains concretely why the two frontiers must be distinguished. This is a motivated first-failure classification rather than an arbitrary finite scan.
